surfaces.name: Rove terminal UI (rove CLI on Bun; macOS, Linux, WSL, native Windows)
Rove desktop window (Electron wrapper around rove --web)
rove api CLI, daemon socket and bridge WebSocket
Rove Mobile iOS remote control (SwiftUI, built from source)
Rove for Android remote control (Kotlin, Compose; built from source)

claims.answer: Terminal UI on macOS, Linux, WSL and native Windows; browser client (rove --web); Electron desktop window (macOS, Windows x64, Linux AppImage); SwiftUI iOS and Kotlin Android remote controls built from source; WeChat bridge. No editor extension.

desktop_os.answer: TUI runs on macOS, Linux, WSL and native Windows (Bun >= 1.3.11, Node and Git Bash on Windows); Electron desktop app builds for macOS arm64/x64, Windows x64 (unsigned) and Linux AppImage. Minimum OS versions are not stated.

mobile_apps.answer: Native SwiftUI iOS app and Kotlin Android app exist as bridge remote controls; both are built from source, iOS lists TestFlight/App Store distribution as not done and notifications only while the app runs.

browser.answer: rove --web serves the full task rail, terminals, files and diffs to a browser; Web Push and home-screen install are supported.

mobile_browser.answer: Web client has a touch-screen message field under the engine terminal, narrow-window Terminal/Files/Diff/Browser views, home-screen install and Web Push on iOS 16.4+.

cli.answer: rove (TUI) and rove api (scriptable verbs) on the installed CLI.

editor_extensions.answer: No VS Code or JetBrains extension; a Claude Code plugin and skill only teach an agent the rove api surface.

task_actions.answer: TUI, web and phone clients can start tasks, type into engine sessions (including answering permission prompts), read diffs, land and delete tasks; TUI adds line-note review and PR creation.

notifications.answer: Inbox, terminal bell and OSC notifications in the TUI, native desktop notifications, Web Push for closed pages, local mobile notifications while the app runs.

cross_device_continuity.answer: One daemon owns tasks and PTYs; TUI, web, desktop and phones attach to the same sessions and machines.

limitations: iOS has no TestFlight or App Store distribution and no push; Android is documented as a draft built from source.

mobile_apps: Native SwiftUI iOS app and Kotlin Android app exist as bridge remote controls; both are built from source, iOS lists TestFlight/App Store distribution as not done and notifications only while the app runs.

claims.answer: Runs the real interactive CLIs: built-in Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Kimi Code, Pi, OMP and IBM Bob; 15 more launch-and-badge contrib engines; custom commands and plugin engines. Mixed engines per task and per fan-out round.

harnesses.answer: claude, codex, copilot, kimi, pi, omp, bob built in; gemini, opencode, cursor-agent, grok, droid, amp, devin, qodercli, cline, kiro-cli, maki, agy (Antigravity), hermes, kilo, mastracode from the contrib catalog.

model_providers.answer: Model is pinned per task in each engine's own flag spelling; providers are whatever the CLI supports (Pi/OMP take provider/id). Rove has no provider layer of its own.

custom_adapters.answer: Custom engines registered in Settings and plugin [[engines]] manifests add any command; adapters promote an engine to built-in.

session_integration.answer: Rove embeds the real interactive CLI in a hosted PTY with hooks, transcripts or screen manifests for activity; it does not use an API wrapper.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Fan-out accepts --agents claude:2,codex:1 and conversations in one directory can use different vendors; a quota-limited task can be switched to another engine on the same branch.

limitations: Model provider choice belongs to each CLI; contrib engines have no login state, history or model picker.
model_providers: Model is pinned per task in each engine's own flag spelling; providers are whatever the CLI supports (Pi/OMP take provider/id). Rove has no provider layer of its own.

claims.answer: Uses each engine CLI's own login, so existing Claude, Codex and Copilot subscriptions or API keys work; Rove shows Claude and Codex subscription windows. No vendor credits.

agent_subscriptions.answer: Each engine runs with its own CLI authentication; account detection reads Claude and Codex plan and reports signed-in state for Copilot, Kimi and Bob.

api_accounts.answer: Engines using API keys work because Rove launches the real CLI with the user's environment; Rove stores no keys.

vendor_credits.answer: Rove sells nothing and has no credit system; bounded search finds no billing or credit code.

local_models.answer: Pi and OMP engines take provider/model patterns, so local providers work only if the CLI supports them; Rove has no local model runtime.

account_switching.answer: Settings shows detected accounts per engine; switching the account is done in the engine CLI.

vendor_account_requirement.answer: No Rove account exists; only the chosen engine CLI needs its vendor account.

provider_restrictions.answer: Provider terms for subscription use inside third-party tools were not checked.

limitations: Account switching and provider restrictions belong to the engine CLIs; Rove does not manage multiple accounts.

claims.answer: curl or npm install, then rove in a repo and press n; needs git and one engine CLI. Directory tasks work without Git; local repos without a remote work; GitHub needs gh for PRs and issues. BYO SSH machines via rove machine add; no managed cloud.

first_task_setup.answer: curl -fsSL https://rove.run/install.sh | sh (or npm/bun/npx), cd your-repo, run rove, press n.

no_git.answer: Directory tasks open any directory with rove . and need not be a git repository.

local_git_without_remote.answer: Managed tasks branch from a local repo ref; land merges back locally; only publish needs a remote.

hosted_git.answer: publish pushes the branch and opens a PR with gh; GitHub Issues page and PR status use gh.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: Quick start lists git, an engine CLI on PATH, Bun, and on Windows Node.js plus Git Bash; rove doctor diagnoses an install.

managed_cloud_setup.answer: No hosted or managed cloud offering; Cloud is a planned roadmap milestone with no work started.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: rove machine add registers an SSH host, verifies it, can install Rove and create a key there, and rove daemon --resident supports a server hub.

limitations: managed_cloud_setup: No hosted or managed cloud offering; Cloud is a planned roadmap milestone with no work started.

claims.answer: rove api exposes create, read, steer, stop, land and publish verbs over CLI, daemon socket and bridge WebSocket with a versioned envelope; inbound signed webhooks fire routines; TypeScript plugin SDK. No MCP server for task control.

cli.answer: rove api <verb> prints one JSON object; rove api schema lists every verb and flag.

api.answer: Daemon unix-socket api.invoke and bridge WebSocket api.invoke share one verb contract with apiVersion.

sdk.answer: @sma1lboy/rove-plugin-sdk is TypeScript sugar for plugin authors (env, CLI, daemon socket client), not a task-control client library.

mcp_server.answer: The only MCP server is internal (rove remote-workspace mcp) for remote file access by an engine; no MCP server exposes tasks to other agents. Agents are taught the CLI via rove skill install.

webhooks.answer: Routines accept a signed inbound webhook; there are no outbound webhooks, though plugins can react to events and routines can notify over WeChat.

operations.answer: Verbs cover add, send, read-output, collect, land, publish, delete, issue-*, routine-*, checkpoint and rewind.

authentication.answer: CLI uses the local daemon socket; bridge uses a shared or per-device token, password sign-in, Cloudflare Access JWT or relay.

stability.answer: apiVersion is reported and rove api schema is the source of truth, but the roadmap lists the Agent API as partly planned and releases land with every merge.

limitations: Roadmap says the Agent API milestone is only partly shipped.

claims.answer: MCP use is inherited from each engine CLI. Rove has first-party and third-party plugins (rove-plugin.toml) adding panes, events, commands, engines and mods, plus a bundled agent skill. Plugins are unsandboxed.

mcp_client.answer: Rove does not implement an MCP client; engines keep their own MCP configuration, and Rove injects an internal rove-files MCP server only for remote workspaces.

plugins.answer: rove plugin search/install; manifest adds panes, event handlers, commands, settings, engines and mods; bundled plugins include kanban and issues.

custom_tools.answer: Plugin commands in any language and custom engine commands.

instructions_import.answer: rove skill install teaches coding agents the rove api loop and per-repo .rove/init-prompt.md and pr-instructions.md customize prompts; other instruction files stay the engine's own.

authentication.answer: Plugin and engine authentication is the plugin's or CLI's own; Rove stores no integration tokens.

permission_scope.answer: Plugin documentation states nothing is sandboxed; plugins run with the user's permissions.

integration_owner.answer: Connections belong to the engine CLI or the plugin; GitHub work goes through the user's gh CLI.

limitations: mcp_client: Rove does not implement an MCP client; engines keep their own MCP configuration, and Rove injects an internal rove-files MCP server only for remote workspaces.

claims.answer: TUI is Bun with OpenTUI React; web client is React and xterm.js; desktop is Electron wrapping the web client; iOS is SwiftUI; Android is Kotlin Jetpack Compose.

desktop_implementation.answer: Desktop window is Electron loading rove --web; the primary UI is a React terminal renderer (@opentui/react) on Bun.

mobile_implementation.answer: iOS app is SwiftUI (packages/rove-ios) and Android app is Kotlin and Jetpack Compose with a bundled terminal web asset.

hybrids.answer: Web client and desktop are web/Electron hybrids; Android bundles npm-locked terminal assets.

implementation_evidence.answer: Package manifests and docs at the pinned commit state the frameworks.

claims.answer: Tasks are created from a prompt in the TUI, web, phone apps, rove api or routines. GitHub Issues can start a task read-only; a first-party Issues/Kanban mod holds a local backlog. The local issue store is authoritative for backlog; no two-way external sync.

local_creation.answer: n in the TUI, + New task in web, rove api add and routines create tasks; Kanban stories are created with n or issue-create.

prompt_intake.answer: First prompt through the dialog, rove api add --prompt/--prompt-file, /?prompt= web URL.

external_import.answer: GitHub Issues page and workitem-* verbs start a task from an issue with the body as an untrusted prompt; a linear-start plugin exists; no import into the local store.

chat_git_triggers.answer: Routine webhooks accept signed GitHub-style POSTs and a WeChat channel exists; no chat or PR comment trigger found beyond those.

authoritative_tracker.answer: The daemon issue store is authoritative for the local backlog; GitHub Issues are read-only through gh.

stable_ids.answer: Local issues have never-reused integer ids per repo; tasks have task ids; a task keeps a linkedWorkItem pointer to the GitHub issue.

sync.answer: Nothing is written back to GitHub and nothing imported into the local store.

supported_edits.answer: Local issues support create, update title/body/status and delete; GitHub issues are read-only.

external_roundtrips.answer: Any change to a GitHub issue requires going to GitHub; Rove only reads.

limitations: Kanban and Issues mods are not installed by default.

claims.answer: No durable task plan object; each task is a workspace with an engine conversation. Plan mode and plans live inside the engine CLI. Diff-review notes persist per task.

plans.answer: Bounded search of tasks, issues and docs finds no plan or acceptance-criteria record; plans are the engine's own feature.

acceptance_criteria.answer: No acceptance-criteria field; issues carry title, body and status only.

editors.answer: Issue title and body are editable in the Kanban drawer; there is no plan editor.

revisions.answer: No revision history for issues or plans.

implementation_links.answer: An issue links to a task with issue-update --task; no link to commits or PRs from the issue.

amendment.answer: A running task can be steered with send or typing, and the issue body can be edited; no formal plan amendment.

restart_persistence.answer: Tasks, issue store, diff notes and worktrees persist on disk across restarts; transcripts belong to the engine.

claims.answer: Tasks nest as parent and child tasks (shared directory or own worktree) with fan-out groups; there are no epics, blockers or readiness gates. Status is a user-set label.

epics.answer: No epic object; issue board has only open/doing/hold/done.

hierarchy.answer: Parent/child tasks one level of nesting in the sidebar (children of children are not documented); fan-out siblings share a groupId.

blockers.answer: Bounded search finds no blocker or dependency model.

readiness.answer: The derived context group (working, waiting-on-you, ready-for-review, landing) reflects engine and PR state, not task dependencies.

enforcement.answer: Nothing blocks dispatch because there are no dependencies.

state_propagation.answer: Deleting a parent promotes children; there is no status propagation from children to parents.

task_to_epic.answer: No epic concept; a child can be added to any task.

identity_retention.answer: Tasks keep id, worktree and history as children are added.

workflow_constraints.answer: No mandatory workflow or preset; status labels are free-form.

instructions.answer: Engines read their own instruction files; Rove supplies a system prompt to managed sessions and .rove/init-prompt.md.

skills.answer: rove skill install bundles a skill for rove api; other skills are the engine's.

project_docs.answer: The repository docs are the engine's to read; Rove has no doc store.

memory.answer: experimental.dispatcher lets sessions file field notes that new sessions on the repo receive.

provenance.answer: Notes record the filing session; no citation model.

correction.answer: A field-notes dialog on the project row menu lets the owner read and delete notes.

deletion.answer: Owner can delete field notes in the dialog.

freshness.answer: A comment in the field-notes dialog warns that a stale note misleads later agents; there is no automatic staleness control.

takeover_continuity.answer: Tasks, worktrees, notes and engine transcripts persist for whoever attaches to the same daemon.

limitations: Field notes are experimental and off by default.

claims.answer: No Rove-owned code search, indexing or knowledge layer; the engine does retrieval. Rove reads images and PDFs as attachments to the first prompt.

code_search.answer: Search page searches tasks and sessions; code search is the engine's.

indexing.answer: No repository index in the pinned release.

external_knowledge.answer: No external knowledge source integration besides GitHub issues.

multimodal_inputs.answer: Drag, paste or paperclip images and PDFs into new session and engine tabs in the TUI and web.

access_scope.answer: Engines see the task worktree; Rove adds no scoping.

api_retrieval.answer: No retrieval API for code or knowledge.

claims.answer: Local issue store with a Kanban board (Backlog, In progress, Parked, Done), edit in a drawer, start a session from a card, and agent issue-* verbs. No labels, assignment, priority, comments or search.

create.answer: n creates a story; issue-create adds one from a shell.

edit.answer: The drawer edits title and description; issue-update changes fields.

prioritize.answer: Doc states no label/type fields and status is the only dimension; board order only.

search.answer: A Search page covers tasks; issue search is not documented.

filter.answer: Board shows one project at a time; tab cycles projects.

archive.answer: Done stays in Done until a future archive flow exists.

reopen.answer: Status can be flipped back to open or hold.

idea_parking.answer: Open and hold issues park ideas without starting an agent.

explicit_dispatch.answer: Starting a session from the card picks engine and workspace and sets doing.

task_session_separation.answer: Issue records are separate from tasks, linked with issue-update --task.

metadata.answer: Id, title, status, created and body only.

durable_states.answer: open, doing, hold, done persisted in the daemon store.

external_tracker_requirement.answer: No external tracker is needed or used for the backlog.

limitations: Kanban/Issues mod is not installed by default.

shared_ids.answer: Agents and humans use the same integer issue ids per repo.

results.answer: Agents can report on tasks, not on issues.

human_visibility.answer: The board refreshes every few seconds so agent moves appear.

attribution.answer: Issue records carry no author or actor.

permissions.answer: No per-agent permissions; any local client can edit.

claims.answer: Many tasks and tabs run concurrently, each in its own PTY under the PTY host; fan-out caps at 10 attempts from a shell and 5 in the TUI composer. Sidebar and Inbox show running, waiting, errored and finished states.

concurrent_sessions.answer: Each tab is its own PTY process in the standalone PTY host.

concurrent_tasks.answer: Tasks each get a worktree and run engines in parallel.

quotas.answer: The only cap is the fan-out cap (10 from shell, 5 from the TUI composer); no per-user quota.

observed_concurrency.answer: The documented demo shows three agents at once, but no measured concurrency limit is stated.

status_visibility.answer: Sidebar status marks, Inbox attention items, derived groups and PR/check chips.

claims.answer: Work is assigned by creating a task with an engine; a dispatcher records who spawned a child; routing is manual or experimental auto-routing tiers. No claims, queues or exclusive ownership.

human_assignment.answer: A human picks the engine and creates the task; no assignee field.

agent_assignment.answer: An agent runs rove api add to give work to another engine; the dispatcher is recorded.

queues.answer: No queue of pending tasks found.

routing.answer: Experimental auto-routing maps a tier to an engine/model/effort; picker design is documented as partial.

duplicate_prevention.answer: workitem-start reuses the task that already exists for a GitHub issue; no general duplicate guard.

ownership_enforcement.answer: Shared children share directories without write coordination, as the docs warn.

claims.answer: Product-supplied delegation: an agent or script runs rove api add (children, fan-out, other engines), send (peer messages with provenance), report and collect, and read-output; replies route to the dispatcher tab. A bundled skill teaches this.

roles.answer: Dispatcher and worker are recorded on each task; children appear under parents.

model_harness_effort.answer: Each child chooses engine, model and effort at creation.

messages.answer: rove api send delivers [ROVE PEER] messages with provenance and reply command.

results_return.answer: Armed prompts return a [ROVE REPORT] line to the dispatcher tab; collect reads group health.

cross_harness.answer: Children can run different engines from their parent.

orchestration_owner.answer: Rove ships the verbs and skill; the coordinator is a third-party CLI session.

activation.answer: rove skill install, then agents with rove on PATH can call rove api; no flag needed.

authentication.answer: Local daemon socket; no extra auth for agents on the same machine.

live_progress.answer: context --text and read-output show state and recent messages.

retained_results.answer: Reports, the child tab transcript and branch remain after completion.

followup.answer: send can follow up a finished task; engines resume by session identity.

invocation.answer: Any shell command or agent in a Rove session.

limitations: Orchestration is CLI-driven; there is no dedicated role UI beyond the sidebar tree and Inbox.

claims.answer: Daemon-owned Routines run cron prompts that create tasks or deliver into an existing tab, with prechecks, script routines, a signed webhook and run history. The enabled routine keeps the daemon alive; no timezone field.

events.answer: A signed webhook and agent event hooks via plugins; no repository event triggers.

recurring_tasks.answer: A routine fires a fresh task, a standing session or an existing tab.

completion_conditions.answer: Prechecks skip idle runs and report-required prompts flag missing reports; no goal loop.

scheduler_location.answer: The daemon on the host machine.

overlaps.answer: Missed-run and restart behavior is described; overlap policy for a still-running routine is limited to standing sessions.

client_independence.answer: Enabled routines keep the daemon up with no TUI attached; a sleeping host does not fire them.

limitations: Runs only while the host is awake; no retries documented.

claims.answer: Typing into the real engine session steers it; Inbox surfaces permission prompts, questions, rate limits, errors, dead engines and missing reports; decision gates ask the owner; closing the tab or deleting the task stops it.

pause.answer: There is no pause verb; the engine's own interrupt applies in its terminal.

stop.answer: Close a tab, reset a terminal or delete a task to end the session; history and worktree remain by default.

resume.answer: Reattach to the session; after reboot Rove relaunches the command and resumes the conversation by engine identity.

steer.answer: Type or rove api send into the running session.

notifications.answer: Inbox, bell, desktop and web push.

pending_decisions.answer: Permission, question and decision-gate items in the Inbox.

escalation.answer: Blocked items sort first; no timed escalation.

visible_errors.answer: Errors and rate limits are Inbox items with auto-resume times.

retained_history.answer: Scrollback ring up to 64MB per session and engine transcripts persist.

parent_child.answer: Sidebar nests child tasks under parents.

attention.answer: Inbox and Kanban badges sort tasks needing a person to the top.

history.answer: Recent tabs and last events only; no cross-task timeline.

workload.answer: Counts of tasks per group in context; no resource view.

growing_epic.answer: A task can gain children, but there are no epics.

natural_language.answer: A coordinating agent can issue rove api calls from natural language; Rove has no built-in natural-language workflow config.

agent_configuration.answer: Engine, model and effort per task and per child.

in_run_changes.answer: Change engine with v in the sidebar; steer by typing.

live_roles.answer: Dispatcher/worker links and group derivation are visible.

discoverability.answer: rove api schema, skill install and docs.

claims.answer: Execution is on the machine running the daemon and PTY host: your laptop, any registered SSH machine or a server running a resident daemon. No vendor cloud. Quitting the TUI or dropping SSH keeps work running on an awake host.

local.answer: Default: engines run locally in worktrees.

byo_remote.answer: rove machine add over SSH; agents can run on the hub with files on the runner or on the machine.

self_hosted.answer: rove daemon start --resident on a server dispatches to registered machines.

managed_cloud.answer: No managed cloud; Cloud is planned.

hybrid.answer: A hub engine with a remote workspace (add --workspace-on) keeps the agent local and files remote.

provisioning.answer: User installs Rove on each machine; machine add can run the install script.

evidence.finding: ADE for the terminal: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and more side by side, one git worktree and branch per task, sessions that outlive the terminal, web/iOS/Android/desktop/WeChat clients, machines over SSH, review with inline notes, Inbox, PR from a task, scheduled Routines, rove api for scripts and agents, plugins; MIT.

evidence.title: Concepts
evidence.locator: Task; Worktree and branch; Terminal Tabs; The issue store; Where things live (L1-252)
evidence.finding: Managed task = worktree + branch + tabs; directory tasks reuse existing directories and need not be git repos; user-set status labels; child tasks; daemon, PTY host and TUI split; local issue store at ~/.rove/issues.json; fan out/fan in.

evidence.title: Sessions: what survives what
evidence.locator: What survives table (L45-62); Why: three processes
evidence.finding: Quitting the TUI, SSH drop or daemon restart keep processes running; reboot or PTY-host death restores up to 64MB scrollback and relaunches the command; sleep is not detach; Rove does not keep a sleeping host awake.

evidence.title: Engines
evidence.locator: Which engines are supported (L16-37); Contrib engines; Picking an engine
evidence.finding: Built-in claude, codex, copilot, kimi, pi, omp, bob; contrib catalog of 15 more CLIs (launch plus screen badge); custom engines and plugin engines; per-task model and effort in the engine's own flags; Claude/Codex quota probes.

evidence.title: Machines
evidence.locator: What this needs; Add a machine
evidence.finding: Register other machines running Rove with rove machine add over SSH; no ports opened, SSH forwards the daemon unix socket; offers to install Rove and create a key on the remote.

evidence.title: Orchestrating many agents
evidence.locator: Task, shared child, or split; Fan out; Read context (L1-120)
evidence.finding: Fan-out rounds with --count/--agents (cap 10 from shell, 5 from TUI), dispatcher/worker report and peer messages, collect, land; context read derives working/waiting/landing groups; git stash caveat.

evidence.title: Routines
evidence.finding: Daemon-owned cron prompts that create a normal task per run; prechecks, script routines, standing session, signed-webhook trigger; schedules use the daemon host timezone; no per-run cost attribution.

evidence.title: Web client
evidence.locator: What it does today; Security; Sign-in modes; Notifications when the page is closed; Limits
evidence.finding: rove --web serves the same daemon state in a browser; device tokens, password, relay presets, Web Push, home-screen install; every lost-work action logged to bridge stderr with device and address.

evidence.title: Desktop app
evidence.locator: Download table; What it does not do
evidence.finding: Electron window that starts the installed rove --web --no-qr and loads it; DMG for Apple silicon and Intel, Windows exe (unsigned) and Linux AppImage; does not bundle the CLI or daemon.

evidence.title: iOS client
evidence.locator: Start the bridge; Pair the phone; Pending iOS features; Not done yet (L360-379)
evidence.finding: SwiftUI remote control over rove-bridge (Tailscale, Cloudflare Access presets); local notifications only while the app runs; TestFlight/App Store distribution and APNs not done; terminal view, not chat.

evidence.title: Android client
evidence.finding: Kotlin and Jetpack Compose client of bridge protocol v1: pairing, attention ordering, terminal tabs, diffs, new tasks, land/delete; built from source with release signing via env variables.

evidence.title: Rove mobile apps privacy policy
evidence.locator: Data received by Rove developers; Permissions
evidence.finding: Mobile apps have no accounts, analytics, advertising or crash reporting and talk only to the user's own bridge; no push service.

evidence.title: Local work tracking
evidence.finding: No external tracker; daemon-owned issue store (status open/doing/hold/done, id, title, body, created) part of the Kanban first-party mod, not installed by default; agents use rove api issue-list/create/update.

evidence.title: TUI guide
evidence.locator: Inbox (L238-290); Diff review (L291-318); Create a PR with the active agent (L373-389); Kanban (L595-651); GitHub Issues (L669-683); Quota in the footer (L808-818)
evidence.finding: Inbox attention items and decision gates; diff review with line notes sent as one prompt; PR creation is an agent prompt running gh; Kanban board of the local issue store; read-only GitHub issues page starting tasks; Claude/Codex quota meters.

evidence.title: rove api reference
evidence.locator: One contract, three transports (L20-50); The orchestration loop (L122-170); lifecycle publish/land (L1967-2040); issues (L1820)
evidence.finding: Scriptable verbs over CLI, daemon socket and bridge WebSocket with apiVersion envelope; send/read-output/collect/land/publish; land refuses dirty base and empty branches, merge or squash.

evidence.title: Configuration
evidence.locator: Experimental (L520-529); First-party mods (L493-503); Per-repo init (L688); Cloned ignored directories (L430)
evidence.finding: Experimental flags (remoteProjects, autoStatus, dispatcher field notes, layerfs); Kanban and Issues mods not installed by default; per-repo .rove/init.sh and clone-dirs; update channels latest/next/nightly.

evidence.title: Quick start
evidence.finding: curl install script (macOS, Linux, WSL), npm/bun/npx; native Windows needs Node.js and Git for Windows with Git Bash; Bun >= 1.3.11; needs git and at least one engine CLI on PATH.

evidence.title: Roadmap
evidence.finding: Dated check against 0.9.282 (2026-11-09): web side panel in progress, distributed core shipped, Agent API planned (first part shipped), Cloud planned with no work started and no date.

evidence.title: Workspace backends and runners
evidence.finding: Design note: git-worktree, borrowed, cow-clone, remote and experimental layerfs workspace backends; checkpoints and rewind landed; dispatch to registered machines landed.

evidence.title: Writing Rove plugins
evidence.finding: Plugins are directories with rove-plugin.toml: panes, event handlers, commands, settings, engines and mods; nothing is sandboxed.

evidence.title: Worktrees
evidence.finding: Per-turn checkpoints as git refs (newest 100 per task), checkpoint-list, checkpoint and rewind verbs, only for managed task worktrees.

evidence.title: MIT License
evidence.finding: MIT License, copyright Jackson Chen, covering the repository.

evidence.title: Rove CLI package manifest
evidence.finding: @sma1lboy/rove 0.9.297, bin rove; dependencies include @opentui/core, @opentui/react, react, xterm headless, ws, smol-toml and yaml; no analytics or telemetry SDK.

evidence.title: rove-web package manifest
evidence.finding: Web client built with React, react-dom and xterm.js (webgl, fit, serialize addons).

evidence.title: PR status monitor
evidence.locator: gh pr view fields; checkStateFromRollup (L21, L102)
evidence.finding: Reads number, url, state, reviewDecision, mergeable and statusCheckRollup through gh and reduces CI checks to a check state shown on tasks.

evidence.title: Derived task group
evidence.finding: Derives waiting-on-you/working/ready groups from engine state, including rate_limited with auto-resume.

evidence.title: Claude quota probe
evidence.finding: Reads the user's Claude OAuth usage endpoint (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage) to show subscription windows and arm auto-resume.

evidence.title: Update check
evidence.finding: Update check fetches the npm registry dist-tag and GitHub release notes; no other first-party endpoint found.

evidence.title: agent-turns handler
evidence.finding: Sums per-turn input and output tokens from the vendor transcript for a task; no currency conversion.

evidence.title: Parallel round planner
evidence.finding: A parallel round larger than the fan-out cap is refused with a spawn-in-batches message.

evidence.title: Experimental LayerFS backend
evidence.finding: Experimental layerfs backend (Linux Runners): task files live in a FUSE-mounted LayerFS workspace run through docker exec; enabled only by experimental.layerfs in state.json.

evidence.title: Cloudflare Access verification
evidence.finding: Bridge verifies a Cloudflare Access JWT (signature, issuer, AUD, expiry) for the cf preset; SSO happens at Cloudflare, not in Rove.

evidence.title: Routine verbs
evidence.finding: routine-create accepts --webhook: signed POST to /hooks/routines/<id> (X-Hub-Signature-256) fires the routine with a generated secret.

evidence.title: Issue board bucketing
evidence.finding: Board columns derive from the issue lifecycle (open/doing/hold/done) and a task link set with issue-update --task.

evidence.title: Decision gates
evidence.finding: An agent raises a decision gate that appears in the owner's Inbox as decision_needed with options; the answer is delivered with the next send.

evidence.title: Remote workspace MCP/hooks
evidence.finding: Internal stdio MCP server and hooks so an engine on the hub reads, writes and edits files on a remote machine's worktree.

evidence.title: Claude Code plugin and skill
evidence.finding: rove skill install places a bundled skill and Claude Code hooks so a coding agent can drive rove api.

evidence.title: GitHub repository API
evidence.finding: Public repository Sma1lboy/rove: 188 stars, MIT license, pushed 2026-11-17 (observed 2026-11-17).

evidence.title: Rove v0.9.297 release
evidence.finding: Stable release v0.9.297 published 2026-11-16 at commit 4a510ee; newer -next prereleases are published for every merge to main.

evidence.title: Bounded search: editor extensions
evidence.locator: ls packages; grep -rniE "vscode|jetbrains|vs code extension" docs packages (excluding node_modules)
evidence.finding: Packages are rove, rove-daemon, rove-bridge, rove-web, rove-desktop, rove-ios, rove-android, rove-weixin, rove-plugin-sdk, rove-harness, rove-docs, rove-landing, branding and promo-kit; no VS Code or JetBrains extension package and no docs mention one.

evidence.title: Bounded search: cost and spend
evidence.finding: No currency cost, budget or spend implementation; token counts exist in handlers-agent-turns.ts and daemon-runtime.ts; quota windows are shown for Claude and Codex only.

evidence.title: Bounded search: roles, SSO, shared users
evidence.finding: Only cf-access.ts (Cloudflare Access JWT) matches; no accounts, organizations, roles, invitations or presence implementation. Auth is a device token or password per bridge.

evidence.title: Bounded search: run limits
evidence.finding: No turn, token or spend limit for agent runs; only the fan-out cap, routine run limits and connect timeouts.

evidence.title: Bounded search: dependencies and blockers between tasks
evidence.finding: No task or issue dependency model; relationships are parent/child (dispatcher, child tasks) only.

evidence.title: Bounded search: living specifications
evidence.locator: grep -rniE "living spec|spec-driven|requirements doc|acceptance criteria" packages/rove*/src docs
evidence.finding: No persistent product specification, acceptance criteria or drift check; the daemon issue store has title, body and status only.

evidence.title: Deletion audit and bridge stderr log
evidence.finding: Daemon records task deletions and the bridge writes destructive actions with device and time to stderr; no general attributed activity history, export or integrity model.
